cases.sentence: Уже давно прошел тот ___, когда по самым верным расчетам людей, знающих эти дела, Китти должна была родить.
cases.translation: The term had long since passed by which, according to the most reliable calculations of people who knew about these things, Kitty was supposed to give birth.
cases.explain: Срок is the subject of the verb прошел (had passed), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Она теперь ясно сознавала зарождение в себе нового ___ любви к будущему, отчасти для нее уже настоящему ребенку.
cases.translation: She now clearly recognized within herself the birth of a new feeling of love for the child still to come, and in part already present for her.
cases.explain: The noun зарождение (the birth/emergence of) governs the genitive case for what is being born, giving чувства.

cases.sentence: ...любви к будущему, отчасти для нее уже настоящему ___.
cases.translation: ...love for the child still to come, who for her was in part already present.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward/for) governs the dative case, giving ребенку.

cases.sentence: В ___ он не любил играть, в клуб не ездил.
cases.translation: He did not like playing cards, and did not go to the club.
cases.explain: The preposition в expressing the target of the game governs the accusative case, giving карту.

cases.sentence: ...она видела..., что он... очень привлекателен своей сильной ___...
cases.translation: ...she saw...that he...was very attractive with his strong figure...
cases.explain: The adjective привлекателен (attractive) governs the instrumental case for the means of attraction, giving фигурой.

cases.sentence: Левины жили уже третий месяц в ___.
cases.translation: The Levins had already been living in Moscow for the third month.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) expressing location governs the prepositional case, giving Москве.

cases.sentence: Кровь прилила к ___, и яркая краска... выступила на лицо.
cases.translation: Blood rushed to her heart, and a bright color came out on her face.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case, giving сердцу.

cases.translation: ...when Kitty, in society, would look at him...
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) expressing location governs the prepositional case, giving обществе.

reading.ru: Левины жили уже третий месяц в Москве.
reading.question: How long had the Levins been living in Moscow?
reading.explain: The text says the Levins had already lived in Moscow for the third month.

reading.ru: Однако Китти чувствовала себя совершенно спокойную и счастливую.
reading.question: How did Kitty feel despite everyone else's anxiety about the birth?
reading.explain: The text says Kitty felt completely calm and happy.

reading.ru: Она теперь ясно сознавала зарождение в себе нового чувства любви к будущему, отчасти для нее уже настоящему ребенку
reading.question: What new feeling did Kitty become clearly aware of?
options: A growing love for her coming child
reading.correct: A growing love for her coming child
reading.explain: The text says she clearly recognized a new feeling of love for the child to come.

reading.ru: Одно, что портило ей прелесть этой жизни, было то, что муж ее был не тот, каким она любила его и каким он бывал в деревне»
reading.question: What was the one thing spoiling Kitty's enjoyment of life in Moscow?
options: Her husband was not the same man she had loved in the country
reading.correct: Her husband was not the same man she had loved in the country
reading.explain: The text says the one thing spoiling her life was that her husband was not the man she had known in the country.

reading.ru: В городе же он постоянно казался беспокоен и настороже, как будто боясь, чтобы кто-нибудь не обидел его и, главное, ее.
reading.question: How did Levin seem to behave in the city?
options: Constantly restless and on guard, as if fearing someone might offend him or Kitty
reading.correct: Constantly restless and on guard, as if fearing someone might offend him or Kitty
reading.explain: The text describes Levin as constantly restless and on guard in the city.

reading.ru: Она видела со страхом даже для своей ревности, что он не только не жалок, но очень привлекателен своей упорядочностью
reading.question: What did Kitty realize about how Levin appeared to others?
options: That he was actually very attractive, not pitiable, which even alarmed her jealousy
That he was seen as awkward and out of place
That other women found him boring
That he was regarded as unintelligent
reading.correct: That he was actually very attractive, not pitiable, which even alarmed her jealousy
reading.explain: The text says she saw, with fear even for her own jealousy, that he was very attractive.

reading.ru: В карту он не любил играть, в клуб не ездил.
reading.question: What did Levin dislike doing in Moscow?
options: Playing cards and going to the club
reading.correct: Playing cards and going to the club
reading.explain: The text says he did not like playing cards and did not go to the club.

reading.ru: И, кроме того, он жаловался ей, что слишком много разговаривал здесь о своей книге, и что потому все мысли о ней спутались у него и потеряли интерес.
reading.question: What did Levin complain about regarding his book?
options: That talking about it too much had confused his thoughts and made him lose interest
That he had lost the manuscript
That no one wanted to publish it
That Kitty did not support his writing
reading.correct: That talking about it too much had confused his thoughts and made him lose interest
reading.explain: The text says he complained that talking too much about his book had confused his thoughts about it and made him lose interest.

reading.ru: В этом отношении случилось даже одно очень важное для них обоих событие, именно встреча Китти с Вронским.
reading.question: What important event happened related to jealousy between Kitty and Levin?
options: Kitty's meeting with her old governess
reading.explain: The text names Kitty's meeting with Vronsky as the important event.

reading.ru: Старуха-княгиня Марья Борисовна, крестная мать Кити, всегда очень ее любившая, пожелала непременно видеть ее.
reading.question: Who wished to see Kitty and led to her encountering Vronsky?
options: Kitty's godmother, old Princess Marya Borisovna
reading.correct: Kitty's godmother, old Princess Marya Borisovna
reading.explain: The text says old Princess Marya Borisovna, Kitty's godmother, wished to see her.

reading.ru: Китти при этой встрече могла упрекнуть себя только в том, что на мгновение, когда она узнала в штатском платье столь знакомые ей когда-то черты, у ней прервалось дыхание.
reading.question: What was Kitty's only reason for self-reproach at seeing Vronsky again?
options: Her breath caught for a moment when she recognized his once-familiar features
She burst into tears in front of everyone
reading.correct: Her breath caught for a moment when she recognized his once-familiar features
reading.explain: The text says her only reproach was that her breath caught for a moment on recognizing him.

reading.ru: Она сказала с ним несколько слов, даже спокойно улыбнулась на его шутку о выборах, которую он назвал «Наш парламент».
reading.question: How did Kitty behave when Vronsky made a joking remark about the elections?
options: She calmly smiled at his joke
She scolded him for the joke
reading.correct: She calmly smiled at his joke
reading.explain: The text says she even calmly smiled at his joke, which he called "Our parliament."

reading.question: How did Kitty feel about her own composure after meeting Vronsky?
options: She was confused about her feelings
She was angry with her father
reading.explain: The text says she herself was pleased with herself.

reading.ru: Левин покраснел гораздо больше ее, когда она сказала ему, что встретила Вронского у княгини Марьи Борисовны.
reading.question: How did Levin react when Kitty told him about meeting Vronsky?
options: He blushed far more than she had
He became furious and left the house
reading.correct: He blushed far more than she had
reading.explain: The text says Levin blushed far more than she did when told of the meeting.

reading.ru: Левин совершенно повеселел и сказал, что он очень рад этому.
reading.question: How did Levin feel after learning all the details of Kitty's meeting with Vronsky?
options: He became entirely cheerful and said he was very glad
He demanded she never see Vronsky again
He decided to leave Moscow immediately
reading.correct: He became entirely cheerful and said he was very glad
reading.explain: The text says Levin became completely cheerful and said he was very glad.
